query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A cryogenic rolling followed by a controlled annealing treatment applied to (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will refine its microstructure into a heterogeneous, hierarchical lamellar architecture that reduces crack initiation and increases load-bearing integrity while preserving the intrinsic caloric phase transformation responsible for its large field‐ and pressure‐induced caloric response. This intervention acts by generating high dislocation densities during severe deformation that, upon annealing, promote heterogeneous nucleation and the development of ultrafine, twin-rich regions.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic or pressure fields but has a coarse microstructure with poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Subject the as-cast alloy to substantial cryogenic rolling (applying severe deformation) followed by a short, optimized annealing treatment (temperature and time selected to induce partial recrystallization and heterogeneous grain refinement).
generation.conditions: Tests performed under the same applied-field (e.g., magnetic fields) and pressure-field conditions as used in its refrigeration applications and at operating temperatures near the caloric phase transition; mechanical loading within service stress levels.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined, hierarchical lamellar microstructure featuring ultrafine recrystallized regions coupled with retained coarser zones and annealing twin boundaries that mitigate stress concentration.
generation.mechanism: Cryogenic rolling introduces high dislocation densities and strain-induced defects that, during annealing, promote heterogeneous nucleation and the development of a composite-like microstructure. The resulting fine-grained and twin-rich regions distribute applied stresses more uniformly and retard crack propagation. Since the treatment primarily alters the microstructure without changing the intrinsic phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect, the caloric performance is expected to remain intact.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in yield strength and ductility (for example, an improvement of approximately 30–50% in mechanical integrity metrics) with significantly reduced cracking tendency, while the magnitude and critical temperature of the caloric response (e.g., magneto- or barocaloric effect) remain within a ±10% range of the original as-cast alloy.
generation.baseline: The unaltered (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits high caloric performance alongside poor load-bearing integrity and a propensity for cracking under load.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness is expected under the specific reversal fields, pressures, and temperature ranges associated with refrigeration operation; if operated outside these regimes (for example, at very high temperatures or under extreme loads), either the mechanical benefits or the caloric response might be compromised.
generation.uncertainty: Precise annealing parameters required to optimize the balance between mechanical improvement and preservation of the caloric transition are not yet established; additionally, the interplay between microstructural refinement and caloric phase stability requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy: one in the as-cast state and one processed using the proposed cryogenic rolling and annealing treatment. Conduct mechanical tests (tensile and fracture toughness measurements) along with caloric performance evaluations (measurement of ΔT, entropy change, and transition temperature under applied magnetic/pressure fields) on both batches under identical operating conditions.
measurements: Caloric temperature change (ΔT) or entropy change during field/pressure cycling
Transition temperature of the caloric phase transformation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (e.g., ≥30% increase) in mechanical integrity metrics without a degradation in the caloric response (i.e., caloric effect magnitude or transition temperature changing by more than ±10% compared to the as-cast alloy), then the hypothesis is falsified.

Possibilities of enhancing mechanical properties of brittle intermetallic containing high entropy alloys (HEAs) using novel processing and microstructural design strategies were investigated in the present work. For this purpose, homogenized CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 HEA consisting of FCC matrix and complex Laves phase particles was successfully processed by severe cold- or cryo-rolling to 90% reduction in thickness followed by annealing (800 °C/1 hour(h)). As compared to cold-rolling, cryo-rolling resulted in a finer lamellar nanostructure and decidedly greater fragmentation of the Laves phase. Upon annealing, the cold-rolled HEA showed a recrystallized FCC matrix dispersed with D019 structured ε nano-precipitates. In contrast, the finer nanostructure and greater driving force for accelerated precipitation of profuse nano-precipitates at the early stages of annealing inhibited recrystallization in the cryo-rolled HEA and resulted in the formation of heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained deformed and recrystallized regions.
